answer: Tie influence to the shape of the vouch graph, not head count. Real trust grows along a trellis of visible work across many unrelated threads, each identity earning its own pigment of style. Sybil farms must vouch for each other, forming dense clusters with mostly internal edges. Weight every attestation by the inverse edge density of its cluster, so a copper-plated ring of fakes earns little unless its members venture out and accumulate cross-cluster vouches, which costs more than any reward.
